advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard _build_and_read_probe against an empty observed vocabulary (raise/fold to `unavailable` when core statuses+types are empty, as build_mapping_layer does) before treating any absence as drift.
evidence: doctor_mapping.py:204-208 `port = mapping_probe.build_probe()` then `statuses = set(port.statuses())` / `types = {...}` / `links = set(port.issue_link_types())` — the getters are called directly, not through build_mapping_layer

mapping_probe.py:308-317 the builder raises ProbeError when `not issue_types and not statuses` ('succeeded-but-observed-nothing … indistinguishable from a broken probe'), a guard the doctor path never reaches

doctor_mapping.py:246-249 `if value not in seen: findings.append(_drift(...))` — every configured value drifts when `seen` is empty, and _drift emits severity 'error' (line 255) which folds into a non-zero exit via has_blocking_mapping

mapping_probe.py:133-136 `def issue_link_types(...)` wraps the call in `self._soft(..., [])` with no `optional=False`, so a failure degrades to `[]` (an empty optional axis is a legitimate observation for the SUGGEST use-case, not for a drift oracle)
doctor_mapping.py:207 `links = set(port.issue_link_types())` accepts the empty set with no distinction between 'Jira has no link types' and 'the link-types call failed'
doctor_mapping.py:246-249 an empty `seen` for the link axis marks every configured link value absent
advisory.finding: The live-drift probe read (_build_and_read_probe) bypasses build_mapping_layer's systemic all-empty guard, so an empty CORE vocabulary — e.g. an anonymous/unauthorized client answering 200-with-nothing — yields empty status/type sets that are indistinguishable from Jira genuinely lacking those values; _drift_findings then reports every configured value as drift, producing false-positive ERROR findings and a spurious non-zero doctor exit.
merged_from: issue_link_types() is a fail-SOFT optional getter that returns [] on any error (e.g. a 403 on that single endpoint); _build_and_read_probe treats that empty set as authoritative, so a transient/permission failure on link types alone makes every configured link value a false drift ERROR.
scenarios: A CI or operator runs `rebar doctor` with jira-datacenter installed and a JIRA_PAT that has lost project-browse permission: Jira returns 200-with-empty status/type lists; doctor reports every configured status/type as drift and exits non-zero.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse build_mapping_layer (or replicate its all-empty ProbeError guard) in _build_and_read_probe so a succeeded-but-observed-nothing probe degrades to a single `unavailable` finding rather than manufacturing per-value drift errors.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a live-drift test: capability installed + injected probe whose observed vocabulary contains the configured status/type/link values, asserting zero `mapping-drift` findings and a non-blocking result.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/doctor_mapping.py:246-249: `for axis, seen in observed_by_axis.items(): for value in sorted(set(resolved[axis].values())): if value not in seen: findings.append(_drift(axis, value, key))`
test_live_drift_per_axis_divergence asserts only divergence findings; no test injects a probe whose observed vocabulary CONTAINS the configured value and asserts zero mapping-drift findings.

Named violating input: config `[mapping.projects.REB.status_map] open = "In Progress"` with a probe whose `statuses()` includes `"In Progress"` must produce NO mapping-drift finding — untested, so an inverted comparison reporting a spurious drift error (non-zero exit) is not caught.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the live-drift CLEAN-SUCCESS path — capability installed, probe returns observed vocabularies, and every configured value is PRESENT in the observed set, so `_drift_findings` returns []. Only the divergence case is tested; an inversion of the `value not in seen` comparison (line 248) or a wrong axis mapping would still pass every existing test.
scenarios: A refactor or logic inversion in `_drift_findings` that flips agreement into a false drift error, breaking the portable happy path once Jira is reachable.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_live_drift_clean_no_findings` injecting a probe port whose vocabularies include the configured target values (e.g. `open = "In Progress"` present in `statuses()`), then `assert [f for f in findings if f['kind']=='mapping-drift'] == []` and `assert not doctor_mapping.has_blocking_mapping(findings)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the `unavailable` finding's `detail` contains the cause-specific prefix (e.g. "Jira backend not configured" for the empty-PAT path, "settings error" for the ConfigError path).
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/doctor_mapping.py:217-220: `if isinstance(exc, BackendEnvError): return f"Jira backend not configured: {exc}" ... if isinstance(exc, ConfigError): return f"settings error: {exc}"`
advisory.finding: The degradation tests assert only the count/severity of the `unavailable` finding, never that its `detail` reflects the tailored cause string produced by `_degrade_reason` (the `BackendEnvError`/`ConfigError` prefixes). The cause-specific branch logic (lines 217-220) is added but its output is unverified.
scenarios: A swap of the two isinstance branches or a broken f-string would still pass, so the user-facing reason strings could regress silently.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the empty-PAT and ConfigError degradation tests, add `assert "Jira backend not configured" in unavailable[0]["detail"]` and `assert "settings error" in unavailable[0]["detail"]` respectively.

evidence: doctor_mapping.py:241 `for key in sorted(cfg.projects):` — the drift loop omits `_DEFAULT_SENTINEL`
doctor_mapping.py:100 the offline tier iterates `[*sorted(cfg.projects), _DEFAULT_SENTINEL]`, establishing that the default layer is a meaningful resolution target

comment at doctor_mapping.py:30-32 states resolve_for_project applies default+builtin for any absent key, so a project inheriting a drifted default value would only be caught if that project key were itself present
dropped.finding: The live-drift tier checks drift only for keys in cfg.projects and never for the default/builtin layer (the _DEFAULT_SENTINEL that the offline tier does exercise), so a [mapping.default.*] value that Jira no longer exposes is never reported as drift.
scenarios: An operator configures [mapping.default.status_map] with a status Jira later renames but declares no per-project block: the offline resolvers pass and live drift never fires, so the drift silently reaches reconcile.
